title: Shorter Is Not Cheaper: A Controlled Comparison of Declarative Animation Specifications and Free-Form Code for LLM-Generated Explanations
abstract: arXiv:2610.32129v1 Announce Type: new  Abstract: Chat assistants increasingly answer conceptual questions with interactive, animated explanations, generated either as free-form HTML/JavaScript or as declarative specifications that a fixed runtime plays. The declarative route is widely expected to be cheaper, faster and more reliable, because its outputs are shorter and constrained. We test this expectation in controlled comparisons whose hypotheses and analysis plans were frozen before the runs. translated_title: 更短并不更便宜：声明式动画规范与自由格式代码在LLM生成解释中的受控比较
translated_abstract: 聊天助手越来越多地使用交互式、动画化的解释来回答概念性问题，这些解释要么以自由格式的HTML/JavaScript代码生成，要么以由固定运行时播放的声明式规范生成。声明式方式被普遍预期更便宜、更快、更可靠，因为其输出更短且受到约束。我们在假设和分析计划均预先冻结的受控比较中检验了这一预期。我们设计了ExplainSpec——一种按时间索引的声明式动画格式，以及一项观察契约，使每个生成的解释都可以被程序化检查；经过验证的、与节奏无关的检查器对来自五个领域的20个解释请求进行评分。三个Claude模型（360个任务）以及后续加入的开源权重Qwen3-14B（分别启用和禁用思考模式，240个任务）以两种格式回答了所有请求。对于每个模型，声明式规范的答案令牌数量缩短了25-48%（摘要在此处被截断）
tldr: 本研究通过预先冻结假设与分析计划的受控实验发现，尽管声明式动画规范的输出比自由格式代码短25-48%，但“更短即更便宜、更可靠”的普遍预期并不成立。
en_tdlr: Through controlled comparisons with preregistered hypotheses and analysis plans, this study shows that the common expectation that declarative animation specifications are cheaper and more reliable because their outputs are shorter does not hold, even though specifications are 25-48% shorter in answer tokens than free-form code.
